gaps: No story makes the accepted mobile-first, installable web app and free-tier hosting constraints testable. All six stories are marked fullstack, but none has an acceptance criterion for phone-browser use from a WhatsApp link, installability, or free-tier operation (plans/roadmap-input.json:31; docs/decisions/0004-mobile-web-free-tier.md:15).

CWF-1 requires consent and version storage but does not require the notice to disclose the data uses, recipients, deletion route, contact address, or backup retention specified for informed consent (plans/roadmap-input.json:39; docs/specs/accounts.md:59).

CWF-1 protects email and Google ID but omits the rule that another member may receive a person's name, WhatsApp number, and cards only while they share a circle, including through direct data requests. Later criteria cover particular circle and search flows without stating this account-wide data boundary (plans/roadmap-input.json:44; docs/specs/accounts.md:89).

CWF-1 has no criterion for viewing one's own profile, including the Google email, or for rejecting an invalid profile edit with a message while preserving the previous value (plans/roadmap-input.json:43; docs/specs/accounts.md:98).
CWF-2 requires an active invite link but omits the minimum 128 bits of randomness needed to prevent guessing (plans/roadmap-input.json:59; docs/specs/circles.md:31).
CWF-2 does not require Share on WhatsApp to prefill the circle name and link, leaving its central sharing action underspecified (plans/roadmap-input.json:59; docs/specs/circles.md:35).

CWF-2 has no criterion that a member can list their circles, see each circle's members and admin, or go straight into a circle when opening its valid link as an existing member (plans/roadmap-input.json:60; docs/specs/circles.md:53; docs/specs/circles.md:72).

CWF-2 records a join event but does not require the new member and existing members to see each other's previously listed cards after joining. CWF-3 covers added and edited cards, leaving the join-time visibility handover unproved (plans/roadmap-input.json:62; plans/roadmap-input.json:90; docs/specs/circles.md:144).

CWF-2 grants removal power without stating that an admin cannot remove themselves, and it omits the rule that no list or names of removed people are shown. Both affect the admin handover and removal privacy behavior (plans/roadmap-input.json:68; docs/specs/circles.md:92; docs/specs/circles.md:108).

CWF-3 says added and edited cards become visible but does not require edits to apply every add rule, reject duplicates or unsafe variants, update matching searches, and disappear from searches matching only the old values (plans/roadmap-input.json:87; plans/roadmap-input.json:90; docs/specs/cards.md:118).

CWF-3 tests corrected bank names on existing cards but omits preservation of search matches and the rule that banks are never removed from the fixed list, leaving saved cards and searches vulnerable to a later list update (plans/roadmap-input.json:95; docs/specs/cards.md:46; docs/specs/cards.md:134).

CWF-4 calls for a prefilled card-only message but does not specify the confirmed message text, and its contact reminder omits that the card holder places the order themselves (plans/roadmap-input.json:115; plans/roadmap-input.json:119; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:64; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:77).

CWF-6 requires per-circle rows but never states their measures or the current member-count column, including that this count is blank for deleted circles. A table containing only circle names would satisfy the roadmap wording (plans/roadmap-input.json:152; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:72).

CWF-6 needs creation time, deletion state, last name, and whether the creator was the owner for later-deleted circles. CWF-2 only preserves past events under the last name, and CWF-5 erases account identity; neither story commits to retaining the non-identifying historical facts needed to calculate CWF-6's new-circle measures after deletion (plans/roadmap-input.json:71; plans/roadmap-input.json:132; plans/roadmap-input.json:151; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:54).
contradictions: The accounts epic promises that members can erase themselves completely, while the confirmed account contract retains anonymous usage events and permits deleted data to remain in provider backups until expiry. The objective overstates the promised erasure (plans/roadmap-input.json:7; docs/specs/accounts.md:120; docs/specs/accounts.md:124).

The accounts epic contains both prerequisite CWF-1 and downstream CWF-5. CWF-2 depends on accounts through CWF-1, while CWF-5 depends on circles and find/contact; the board derives epic-level blockers from every story edge and therefore reports accounts and circles/find-contact as blocking each other even though the story graph can advance (plans/roadmap-input.json:49; plans/roadmap-input.json:76; plans/roadmap-input.json:139; factory/scripts/forge_cli/board.py:555).

CWF-6 says a deleted-then-recreated owner loses access until configuration names a new Google account ID, but CWF-1 and its source spec identify the same Google account by its stable account ID across sign-ins. Signing up again with that Google account supplies the configured ID again, so this acceptance criterion cannot pass as written (plans/roadmap-input.json:37; plans/roadmap-input.json:157; docs/specs/accounts.md:24; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:25).
resolutions: CWF-1 gains a criterion for phone-browser use from a WhatsApp link, home-screen installability and free-tier hosting.
CWF-1 gains the privacy-notice content criterion.
Account-wide boundary added: CWF-2 for name and number, CWF-3 for cards, including direct data requests.
CWF-1 profile criterion covers viewing, invalid-edit rejection and keeping the previous value.
CWF-2 gains the 128-bit invite code criterion.
CWF-2 share criterion requires the circle name and link prefilled.
CWF-2 gains circle list, member list and admin display, and existing members go straight to the circle.
CWF-3 requires join-time mutual visibility of previously listed cards (cards exist only from CWF-3).
CWF-2 states the admin cannot remove themselves and no removed-people list or names are shown.
CWF-3 edits apply all add rules; CWF-4 covers search reflection of adds, edits and removals.
CWF-3 states banks are never removed; CWF-4 states bank-name corrections do not change matches.
CWF-4 criteria carry the exact message text and the holder-places-the-order reminder.
CWF-6 per-circle criterion lists its measures and the member-count column, blank for deleted circles.
CWF-2 requires deleted circles to keep last name, creation time, deletion and whether the owner created it.
Accounts epic objective no longer promises complete erasure; the new deletion epic describes removal from the live app and of event identity.
CWF-5 moved to a new account-deletion epic so epic gating derived from story edges has no cycle.
The Usage metrics spec was wrong: a same-Google-account re-signup keeps the configured ID. Spec amended (re-saved as draft, fresh spec grill) and CWF-6 criterion changed to match.
